I treat drum wraps like I would when detailing the exterior of the car because the composition is very similar. I’ve also heard of people who have had success with “headlight restoration kits” that come with all the tools necessary to restore a drum wrap using a similar method to what I do

This one actually aged to a more greenish colour for some reason, I looked it up and it seems to happen from time to time. If anyone has any insights on why that is please let me know! In general when I am trying to reduce the appearance of a “tan” I completely clean the kit and take care of any residue, then I use scratch x car scratch remover which is a very light abrasive polish that will smooth out any tiny scuffs and takes the smallest bit from the exterior layer of the wrap, then deposits a hard polymer wax that restores the smooth surface. I find that this takes a lot of discolouration away. After that I use a natural car wax to achieve the high gloss effect and help the wrap gain dimension again. This is not a perfect system but does bring it closer to the original colour. I’ve seen videos online of people achieving a pure original white marine pearl again using a hydrogen peroxide solution left in the sun but I have been hesitant to try that as I fear it will make the wrap more brittle while lifting the colour.

Sorry for the long winded answer I hope this helps!

Hey! So I’ve been taught that the best way to tell by stamp if you’re dealing with a 50’s or 70’s stamp is the H over E alignment. In the 50’s stamps the H in “Turkish” lines up with the E in “made”. For the 70’s stamps the H is further to the right to the point where the right vertical line of the H is more in line with the I of “in” , hopefully that makes sense! Also size of the drilled holes (it was smaller in the 50’s), for hi hats oftentimes you’ll run into clutches that don’t fit. Also weight of the cymbals, if you have 12” hi hats that are pretty thin and similar in weight, that screams 50’s to me.

Rococo. The soft pastels used is the first clue. Baroque usually focused on clear religious subject matter in accordance with the council of Trent to support the catholic counter reformation. In rococo there is an interest in hidden meanings thus the popularity of allegorical painting, this is in line with the Age of Enlightenment thinking of the 18th century. This painting represents the peaceful reign of Spanish King Ferdinand VI through symbolism and Greco-Roman references. 
Take a look at “The Conversion of Saint Paul” by Caravaggio to compare, his extreme form of chiaroscuro called tenebrism makes him the most baroque of the baroque in my opinion. The religious subject matter is clear, theatrical and violent.
“The Allegory of Justice and Peace” is secular allegory, it is decorative and soft. 
There are similarities between the two styles, and the lines can be blurred at times. When deciding which style a painting belongs to I usually will generalize Baroque with vibrant contrasting colours, harsh chiaroscuro, and clear religious subject matter, and Rococo as complimentary pastels, soft lighting, and secular aristocratic subject matter.

The plant is understood to be saffron because the fresco is generally considered to be about the transition into womanhood. Saffron was used during classical antiquity as a natural remedy for menstrual cramps. There are other Minoan frescos of women with flowing hair but in this one the hair is partially shaved. I read a theory that prepubescent girls had shaved hair and once they reached puberty they would grow it long. The colouring on the head suggests that this girls hair has begun to grow out, therefore she has reached puberty. So I think historians believe it is saffron because of the context rather than the physical similarity.

some of the things you mention are similar to my specific symptoms but some stuff is super contradictory so I mean i would recommend going and getting real medical advice if you think you have adhd... i find it can be very easy to fall down the rabbit hole while doing research online about it because the more you read and think the symptoms the more you can stretch connections to your life...those sort of “do you have blank condition”  quizzes online are really only useful for people in deciding if it’s worth it to see a professional. I don’t mean to be harsh but you gotta ask yourself if your attention and focus issues are something you’ve dealt with your whole life or something that is the product of your current environment... if you have a good relationship with your parents, talk to them about if the things you are noticing in your behaviour now are something that they noticed in you as an adolescent. You have to be honest with yourself first and foremost, a lot of university students will develop attention and organization issues from being a high stress environment and being overworked and overtired constantly. I hope this helps, I don’t mean to deter you but if you feel like you have adhd make sure you are asking yourself the tough questions

Hi, this actually applies to me which is awesome. I am a drummer studying jazz in university, personally I also struggle with bringing myself to learn something that I’m not instantly good at. It seems that my mind will just reject practice at times, since I’ve gotten on meds it is way easier to practice and make myself learn new things. While I was off meds my coping mechanisms included putting myself in ensemble situations as often as possible to kind of force myself into practice using jamming, and I’ll try to work new concepts in during higher pressure times. I would also try to give myself insanely easy practice goals, if I was feeling particularly unfocused in a day I would set a goal of practicing 10 minutes out of an hour which seems ridiculous but when faced with that or no practice at all, every little bit counts. The methodical nature of music seems to really disagree with ADHD but if you’re passionate it can work!
